instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Higher education institution with 8,000 students across undergraduate and master's programs in business, engineering, and health sciences. Developing hybrid learning capabilities and micro-credential programs for executive education. Key challenge is student retention analytics and personalized learning pathway design.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have a mature innovation program with a dedicated R&D lab of 12 engineers, an annual innovation budget equivalent to 5% of revenue, and a structured stage-gate process for evaluating and funding new initiatives. In the past 3 years we have launched 4 new product lines that now contribute 18% of total revenue, including an AI-powered recommendation engine that has become our fastest-growing SKU.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base – our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.additionalContext: The shift towards skills-based learning demands constant technological adaptation, specifically integrating generative AI to scale personalized content creation. Internally, the culture struggles with formalized cross-functional collaboration necessary for rapid prototyping and experimentation.
answers.teamSize: The founder handles all product and technology decisions personally with occasional input from a part-time freelance developer. There is no formal engineering team — technical work is either done by the founder or outsourced to contractors on a project basis. Innovation bandwidth is essentially limited to whatever the founder can personally drive alongside day-to-day operations.

opportunities.title: B2B Corporate Skills Marketplace Platform
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging our proprietary micro-credential technology to create a B2B platform allowing corporations to source specialized training modules directly from Beacon Consulting. This radical shift addresses the single product category dependency by targeting a new, high-volume market segment.

first_actions: Conduct pilot interviews with 5 target corporate HR departments.
Develop a Minimum Viable Offering (MVO) focusing on one high-demand skill gap (e.g., prompt engineering).
resources_needed: Contract for specialized B2B SaaS development team
Dedicated marketing budget for enterprise outreach
execution_plan.success_metric: Secure 3 paying corporate pilot customers within 6 months.
milestones: Month 1: Pilot scope finalized and MVP defined.
Month 4: Beta launch with first 2 corporate clients.

opportunities.title: Executive Micro-Specialization Tier
opportunities.rationale: Expanding the existing executive education offerings by developing highly niche, high-value micro-credentials tailored for specific industry verticals (e.g., FinTech compliance). This builds on our existing core strength and increases average transaction value.

first_actions: Identify three underserved industry sectors with demonstrated high learning needs.
Create curriculum framework and secure faculty expertise.
resources_needed: Small marketing spend focused on professional network targeting
execution_plan.success_metric: Increase average course price by 25% within the next fiscal year.
milestones: Quarter 1: Curriculum design completed for two new niche programs.
Quarter 2: Launch of first specialized cohort.

next_steps.action: Establish a cross-functional 'Innovation SPRINT' team to validate the B2B Marketplace concept.
Audit current operational bottlenecks (e.g., curriculum delivery, student onboarding) to identify immediate incremental improvements.

key_weaknesses: Owner-centric decision-making limits the speed and breadth of radical idea execution.
Lack of dedicated, formalized innovation budget constrains experimentation beyond core product maintenance.
High dependency on a single revenue stream (concentrated customer base) creates significant market vulnerability.
